PullRequest.Title: Improve Agent Merge status presentation
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
- show a normal open pull request icon when enabled Agent Merge owns the active PR blockers, while respecting effective per-session repair actions
- observe Agent Merge client state lazily with cached, error-aware session subscriptions and idle retention
- render Agent Merge state notices by hiding only their carrier request while keeping the notification response visible across live and restored sessions

## Validation
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- 300 provider and Agent Merge UI tests
- 404 chat model, persistence, adapter, and view tests
- focused Agent Host live, deferred, and restored notice tests
- Claude Opus 5 code review

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed row-to-subscription call path and cold restore behavior are explicit in the repository. The exact number of simultaneously rendered blocked rows varies by viewport and user history, which affects magnitude but not the per-row fan-out mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: One wire subscription and potentially full session restoration (database/filesystem and git-state work) per distinct rendered blocked Agent Host session
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows linearly with the number of visible session rows carrying git-pull-request-error or git-pull-request-comment icons; same-session consumers are refcount-coalesced, but separate rows target separate session resources and are launched concurrently.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: A burst of Agent Host IPC and restoration I/O, increasing host contention and resource usage when opening or scrolling the sessions list
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Session row rendering selected the cached PR icon without reading Agent Merge state, so rendering inactive rows issued no Agent Host session subscriptions or cold restores.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Rendering each blocker-icon row now observes Agent Merge configuration, which retains a full session-state subscription for that row's session.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line 979 creates and observes an Agent Merge configuration observable inside each blocker-row render autorun; that observable's new provider implementation acquires a StateComponents.Session subscription on first observation.
Findings.Title: Do not cold-subscribe every blocked session row
Findings.Impact: Opening the sessions list with many inactive sessions whose cached PR icon is a blocker now starts one Agent Host session subscription per rendered blocked row. For evicted sessions, each subscription can restore the full session and trigger git-state refresh, creating a burst of IPC plus server filesystem/database work that can contend with list interaction and other Agent Host work.
Findings.Evidence: The added row autorun calls getSessionAgentMergeConfigurationObservable for every rendered row with a PR error/comment icon. That reaches BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider.getAgentMergeClientStateObservable, whose first observer calls _keepAgentMergeSessionStateAlive and then connection.getSubscription(StateComponents.Session, ...). AgentSubscriptionManager sends a wire-level subscribe for each distinct resource, and AgentService.subscribe restores an uncached session and starts a git-state refresh. References coalesce only for the same session; distinct rows remain distinct cold subscriptions, with no aggregate limiter.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep list rendering off the full-session subscription path. Project the small enabled/overrides state into already-loaded session catalog data, or fetch it through a batched/limited list-level mechanism; at minimum avoid launching unbounded cold subscriptions directly from per-row autoruns.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or scroll the sessions list containing inactive Agent Host sessions with cached pull-request blocker icons
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The row renders immediately from cached session/PR data, but the added Agent Merge-aware icon read immediately starts state acquisition; the corrected icon waits for the subscription snapshot. Cold restore work is asynchronous but competes with the interactive list and Agent Host work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON-RPC StateComponents.Session subscribe and full session snapshot transfer
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold call per distinct rendered blocker row; typically viewport-sized, with no batching across sessions
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Row rendering used the cached PR icon and made no Agent Host state subscription.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial DOM paint but launched during row rendering; the Agent Merge-aware icon update depends on completion and the burst competes with foreground host work

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore an evicted session from persisted state and lazily refresh git state
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once for each subscribed row whose session snapshot is not resident; git probing can also occur per restored session
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening or scrolling the list did not restore inactive sessions merely to choose their icon.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Server-side work is required before the subscription snapshot returns and consumes I/O/CPU concurrently with the sessions UI

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct rendered rows whose icon is git-pull-request-error or git-pull-request-comment; same-session consumers deduplicate, but separate rows remain separate resources.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One subscription is launched per distinct qualifying row with no cross-session limiter. IAgentConnection refcounts duplicate consumers of the same resource only.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: WeakMap observables deduplicate per ISession and provider observables deduplicate per session ID. Existing live subscriptions are refcount-shared; cold evicted sessions require a wire subscribe and restore. Unobserved Agent Merge subscriptions are retained for 30 seconds, then released.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added row read, lazy-observable first-listener hook, wire subscribe, and cold restore path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Viewport size, blocker prevalence, and server cache residency vary; warm or already-open sessions collapse to cheap refcount acquisitions, while a cold history with many blocked sessions realizes the fan-out.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium boundary fan-out because a presentation-only per-row read can concurrently cold-load full sessions.

Scenarios.Scenario: View an active session's pull-request pill and CI/review input banners while changing effective Agent Merge actions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Banner generation uses local feedback and live shared PR/CI observables. Refresh calls are fire-and-forget; actions can display from cached/fallback data while network refresh proceeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GitHub pull-request and review REST refresh, plus CI polling when CI remains user-owned
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to two PR metadata requests per unique PR refresh every 60 seconds, plus one CI request per unique PR/head when fixCI is not handled; shared with the header pill and other consumers
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Any enabled Agent Merge state suppressed banner-owned polling; partial overrides can now retain polling only for blockers the user still owns.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous and not required for initial banner paint; live status updates arrive later

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct pull requests attached to the active session, usually one; model references group consumers by owner/repo/PR/head SHA.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: PR refresh performs two parallel GitHub requests, but references, in-flight refreshes, and polling schedulers are shared per PR. Multiple UI consumers increment a polling client count rather than creating multiple recurring loops.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: PR, CI, and review-thread models are reference-counted and shared. In-flight refreshes coalesce; polling remains one scheduler per model. Agent Merge configuration is cached per ISession.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the network calls and model coalescing; exact overlap depends on which metadata pills are instantiated.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A transient immediate refresh can occur on configuration transitions, but in the normal active-session view the header pill already owns the same shared PR models and recurring polls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the changed partial-action behavior is intentional, cardinality is per unique PR, and recurring network work is coalesced by shared models.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show Agent Merge controls and PR presentation for the active session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The controls and icon can render from defaults/cached state; live enabled/override state arrives through the session observable. Global configuration reads are local.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire Agent Host session state for Agent Merge enabled/override presentation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one wire subscription for the active session and commonly zero additional wire calls because the chat handler already subscribes
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Actions listened to provider config events and read cached state without creating this dedicated observable acquisition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Live state affects presentation after arrival but does not block construction of controls

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active session, with multiple UI consumers sharing the same per-session observable and connection resource.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most one session subscription resource; the active chat handler normally already holds it, so acquisition is refcount-only.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The WeakMap and provider Map reuse observables; the connection refcounts the existing subscription. A sole observer keeps it live and idle release applies after the last observer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for refcount coalescing and one-session scope.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Whether a new wire request occurs depends on active-chat subscription timing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression due to same-resource coalescing and constant cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change Agent Merge global or per-session settings and persist configuration notices into monitored transcripts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration changes synchronously scan loaded sessions as before; the diff additionally computes effective behavior and emits a local completed notice turn only for monitored sessions whose effective behavior changed. Notice persistence is not needed for the setting mutation itself.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Record a host-owned local notice turn for later transcript restoration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one notice per qualifying monitored session per effective settings transition
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Configuration changes resynchronized sessions but did not persist explanatory configuration-change turns.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Additional persistence follows a rare explicit configuration change and is not on routine rendering/input paths

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of loaded monitored sessions whose effective configuration actually changes, not total transcript items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The root-config listener iterates sessions synchronously; notice dispatch is per qualifying session and active turns queue notices until idle.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: _announcedConfigurations stores one effective configuration per monitored session and suppresses unchanged notices; entries are removed on disable/session removal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for per-session notice creation and suppression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users may retain many monitored sessions, but settings changes are infrequent and unchanged effective configurations are filtered.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: bounded by explicit settings transitions and required for the new transcript behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load, restore, and render Agent Merge system-notification turns in chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: History conversion and chat-model restoration synchronously carry one extra boolean. Rendering a collapsible notice parses/renderers the short summary and detail Markdown eagerly, while the transcript list controls which response rows are mounted.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of Agent Merge notices in the loaded transcript; each notice has a short bounded set of configuration lines.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous per rendered notice; no subprocess, IPC, database, filesystem, or network call is introduced in the renderer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Request-hidden state persists in serialized chat data and restores directly; no growing cache or missing cleanup is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for allocation/render behavior and absence of an external boundary in the changed renderer.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very long-lived sessions can accumulate notices, but generation is tied to explicit settings transitions and the added content is bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable rendering or serialization regression; the extra work is small, bounded, and only for rendered notices.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 40 changed files. One medium boundary-fan-out issue was reported for per-row cold Agent Host subscriptions; active-session subscriptions, GitHub polling, notice persistence, and chat rendering were traced and found bounded, shared, or off hot paths.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
